summary: The SCREENS Act requires the federal government to establish a national, machine-readable framework for cancer screening recommendations based on data and guidelines from groups like the United States Preventive Services Task Force and the National Cancer Institute. It directs health information technology to incorporate these computable guidelines, sets privacy protections for patient data, requires guidance for health plans to integrate this technology, and permits the Patient-Centered Outcomes Research Institute to support related research and pilot projects.

affected_groups.effect: The National Coordinator, the Secretary of Health and Human Services, and other health agencies must establish frameworks, issue guidance, update certification rules, and consult with stakeholders.
Must include functionality that operationalizes the national computable-guideline framework as a condition of certification within five years.
affected_groups.group: Health information technology developers and certified programs

affected_groups.effect: Will receive guidance encouraging them to integrate technology that operationalizes the cancer screening recommendations and enable consumer opt-ins.
Will have access to consumer-focused, patient-forward technologies and clear information on how their data is used, alongside protections for their personal health information.

key_provisions: Requires the National Coordinator for Health Information Technology to establish an annual national computable-guideline framework for cancer screening recommendations within one year of enactment.
Mandates that the screening recommendations be publicly available in machine-readable screening logic interoperable with mCODE or USCDI datasets.
Enforces privacy protections compliant with HIPAA and prohibits unauthorized use or re-identification of individually identifiable health information.
Requires the Secretary, within five years, to update certification conditions so certified health information technology includes functionality operationalizing the cancer screening recommendations.
Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to issue guidance within two years to encourage health plans to integrate this technology and allow consumer opt-ins.

Authorizes the Patient-Centered Outcomes Research Institute to support research, pilot projects, and implementation activities advancing interoperable health information technology for preventive care.
missing_information: Specific funding amounts or appropriations authorized by the bill.
Penalties for non-compliance with the health IT certification conditions or health plan guidance.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The SCREENS Act requires the federal government to establish a national, machine-readable framework for cancer screening recommendations based on data and guidelines from groups like the United States Preventive Services Task Force and the National Cancer Institute. It directs health information technology to incorporate these computable guidelines, sets privacy protections for patient data, requires guidance for health plans to integrate this technology, and permits the Patient-Centered Outcomes Research Institute to support related research and pilot projects.
summary_detail.significance: The bill establishes a standardized, machine-readable national framework for cancer screening recommendations, altering federal health IT certification requirements and encouraging health plan integration to make preventive screening data more accessible to patients and interoperable across health systems.
